title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #20

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What should you do before acting on a spoken instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh
   B. Move at once
   C. Look away
   D. Listen to all of it

2. What is the plural of the English word loaf? (1 mark)
   A. loafes
   B. loaf
   C. loaves
   D. loafs

3. Singular means (1 mark)
   A. half
   B. many
   C. one
   D. none

4. Vocabulary means (1 mark)
   A. only names
   B. the pictures in a book
   C. all the words you know and can use
   D. only long words

5. Which of these is a cultural food word? (1 mark)
   A. window
   B. pencil
   C. ruler
   D. porridge

6. What is a good way to give feedback to a reader? (1 mark)
   A. Say they are bad
   B. Laugh at mistakes
   C. Say one good thing and one thing to improve
   D. Say nothing

7. How should you sit when you write? (1 mark)
   A. With your back turned
   B. Standing on the chair
   C. Straight, with your book in front of you
   D. Lying on the desk

8. Why should you not rush the last lines of a page? (1 mark)
   A. The page will run away
   B. The pen will break
   C. It is not allowed
   D. Neatness can be lost when you hurry

9. What should you leave between two words? (1 mark)
   A. A finger space
   B. A whole line
   C. No space
   D. A picture

10. What can a weather forecast tell us? (1 mark)
   A. What the weather will be like
   B. Who will win a race
   C. How old we are
   D. What we will eat

11. Which sentence gives information but not an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Today the sky is cloudy.
   B. Bring the clothes.
   C. Close the window.
   D. Stay indoors.

12. Fluent reading needs (1 mark)
   A. only loudness
   B. smooth pace, correct words and good expression
   C. only speed
   D. only a quiet voice

13. How many full stops are needed in: The sky is dark. Rain is coming. (1 mark)
   A. Two
   B. One
   C. None
   D. Three

14. Why do we use punctuation marks? (1 mark)
   A. To use up ink
   B. To make writing clear
   C. To hide meaning
   D. To make pages heavy

15. Which question word asks for a reason? (1 mark)
   A. Why
   B. Who
   C. Where
   D. When

16. In a written dialogue the speaker's name usually comes (1 mark)
   A. in the middle of a word
   B. at the start of the line
   C. at the end
   D. on a different page

17. What do we do in a matching game with words? (1 mark)
   A. Match each word with its meaning
   B. Sing a song
   C. Count the cards
   D. Draw a picture only

18. Which word shows the last step in a sequence? (1 mark)
   A. First
   B. Begin
   C. Next
   D. Finally

19. Which sentence should come first when making tea? (1 mark)
   A. Finally, serve the tea.
   B. First, boil the water.
   C. Next, drink it.
   D. Then pour the milk.

20. Which order is correct? (1 mark)
   A. Eat, go, wash, wake up
   B. Wash, go, wake up, eat
   C. Wake up, wash, eat breakfast, go to school
   D. Go to school, wake up, wash, eat

21. A saying such as It is raining cats and dogs means (1 mark)
   A. the weather is cold
   B. animals are falling
   C. it is raining very heavily
   D. dogs and cats are lost

22. Why should you plan before writing a story? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. To finish early
   C. To organise your ideas
   D. To avoid a title

23. What is the subject of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. Who or what the sentence is about
   B. The full stop
   C. What is said about it
   D. The verb only

24. Which of these is a preposition? (1 mark)
   A. banana
   B. jump
   C. behind
   D. quickly

25. Which is a poem's mood if it is joyful? (1 mark)
   A. Sad
   B. Angry
   C. Happy
   D. Sleepy

26. Which is a constructive leisure activity? (1 mark)
   A. Fighting
   B. Harming others
   C. Reading a book
   D. Wasting money

27. What does an interjection show? (1 mark)
   A. A place
   B. A number
   C. A sudden feeling
   D. A time

28. Which line is written correctly? (1 mark)
   A. Hurray Amina: it is Saturday
   B. Amina Hurray! It is Saturday
   C. Amina: Hurray! It is Saturday.
   D. It is Saturday Amina Hurray

29. Why do writers use interjections in dialogues? (1 mark)
   A. To show feelings and make speech natural
   B. To make it longer
   C. To hide the story
   D. To fill the page

30. What is good telephone manner? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking with food in your mouth
   B. Speaking clearly and giving your name
   C. Interrupting
   D. Calling very late for no reason

31. Which is the last part of a telephone conversation? (1 mark)
   A. Greeting
   B. Asking for a favour
   C. Giving your name
   D. Saying goodbye

32. What does interpret mean? (1 mark)
   A. To tear it
   B. To explain what something means
   C. To sell it
   D. To hide it

33. Which is a difference between an advert and a news item? (1 mark)
   A. An advert tries to sell and news reports facts
   B. News is always a poem
   C. They are exactly the same
   D. Adverts report elections only

34. What is a quote in news? (1 mark)
   A. A map
   B. A price
   C. A drawing
   D. The exact words of a person

35. Where should your class keep collected forms? (1 mark)
   A. In the river
   B. Under a stone
   C. In the fire
   D. In a portfolio

36. What is a digital form? (1 mark)
   A. A paper airplane
   B. A form on a tree
   C. A form made of clay
   D. A form filled in on a device

37. What is polite when you want to speak in a discussion? (1 mark)
   A. Raise your hand or signal
   B. Snatch the talking stick
   C. Shout
   D. Stand on a chair

38. Which is the first step in understanding a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Tear it
   B. Ignore it
   C. Copy it
   D. Read the title and the poem aloud

39. Which is the correct order for washing hands? (1 mark)
   A. Dry, wet, soap, rinse
   B. Wet, rub soap, rinse, dry
   C. Rinse, dry, wet, soap
   D. Soap, dry, wet, rinse

40. In writing, what is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. A poem
   B. Words telling someone what to do
   C. A picture
   D. A story

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain the difference between skimming and scanning. (2 marks)

42. Put the steps in order: (a) Finally, serve. (b) First, boil water. (c) Next, add tea leaves. (3 marks)

43. Correct this paragraph: it was a cold morning in nyeri the children wore sweaters scarves and socks (4 marks)

44. Explain how the position game is played with objects on a table. (4 marks)

45. Describe your favourite leisure activity using the who, where, when and why frame. (3 marks)

46. Describe the steps for creating a form for your class about favourite cultural foods. (5 marks)

47. Explain what intonation is and give one English example of a rising voice. (2 marks)

48. List three ways of taking good care of a domestic animal. (3 marks)

49. Describe how to read a passage with interjections aloud. (4 marks)

50. Give two conjunctions used to join sentences. (2 marks)

51. State two uses of a full stop and a capital letter in a sentence. (2 marks)

52. Give three rules for writing clear instructions. (3 marks)

53. Write two compound sentences about shopping using so and but. (4 marks)

54. Name three headings in a story plan. (3 marks)

55. Explain what attentive listening means. (2 marks)

56. Write the verbs in this instruction: Close the door and sit down. (2 marks)

57. Describe how a panel discussion is organised. (4 marks)

58. Name two prepositions used to show position. (2 marks)

59. Explain what a dialogue is. (2 marks)

60. Give two features of a poem. (2 marks)

61. Give two reasons why we read fluently. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #20 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Listen to all of it
   Listening to the end helps you act correctly.

2. C — loaves
   Loaf changes f to ves in the plural.

3. C — one
   A singular noun names one person, animal, place or thing.

4. C — all the words you know and can use
   Vocabulary is a person's collection of words.

5. D — porridge
   Porridge is a food. The others are not.

6. C — Say one good thing and one thing to improve
   Kind and useful feedback helps people improve.

7. C — Straight, with your book in front of you
   Good posture helps neat writing.

8. D — Neatness can be lost when you hurry
   Careful writing should stay the same to the end.

9. A — A finger space
   A finger width keeps words clear.

10. A — What the weather will be like
   A forecast predicts the weather.

11. A — Today the sky is cloudy.
   It only tells about the weather.

12. B — smooth pace, correct words and good expression
   These are the parts of fluency.

13. A — Two
   There are two sentences, so two full stops.

14. B — To make writing clear
   Punctuation helps readers understand.

15. A — Why
   Why asks the reason.

16. B — at the start of the line
   The name shows who speaks.

17. A — Match each word with its meaning
   The game links words to meanings.

18. D — Finally
   Finally is used for the last step.

19. B — First, boil the water.
   Boiling water is the first step.

20. C — Wake up, wash, eat breakfast, go to school
   This is the natural order of a morning routine.

21. C — it is raining very heavily
   It is an expression for heavy rain.

22. C — To organise your ideas
   A plan gives your story a clear shape.

23. A — Who or what the sentence is about
   The subject is the topic of the sentence.

24. C — behind
   Behind shows position.

25. C — Happy
   A joyful poem has a happy mood.

26. C — Reading a book
   Constructive activities build people up.

27. C — A sudden feeling
   Interjections show emotions.

28. C — Amina: Hurray! It is Saturday.
   It has name, colon and words.

29. A — To show feelings and make speech natural
   Interjections show emotions.

30. B — Speaking clearly and giving your name
   Clarity and courtesy help.

31. D — Saying goodbye
   Calls end with a goodbye.

32. B — To explain what something means
   To interpret is to explain meaning.

33. A — An advert tries to sell and news reports facts
   Their purposes differ.

34. D — The exact words of a person
   A quote repeats what someone said.

35. D — In a portfolio
   A portfolio keeps them organised.

36. D — A form filled in on a device
   Digital forms are filled on phones or computers.

37. A — Raise your hand or signal
   Signal politely.

38. D — Read the title and the poem aloud
   Reading aloud comes first.

39. B — Wet, rub soap, rinse, dry
   This is the logical order.

40. B — Words telling someone what to do
   Instructions say what to do.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: Skimming is quick reading for the main idea and scanning is quick searching for a specific fact.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: b, c, a
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct position.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: It was a cold morning in Nyeri. The children wore sweaters, scarves and socks.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four corrections: capitals at the start, Nyeri, the full stops and the commas.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: One pupil gives an instruction such as put the pencil on the book. Another follows it. The class checks whether the position is correct. Then the roles are swapped.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Any clear description that says the activity, where and when it is done, with whom and why you like it.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for activity, place or time, and reason.

46. (5 marks)
   Answer: Decide the purpose, write a title, list questions such as name, class and favourite food, leave space for answers, write short instructions, test it with a friend and improve it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step up to five.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice as we speak. A question such as Are you coming? rises at the end.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one mark for a correct example.

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: Give food and clean water, provide a shelter, take it to a veterinary doctor when sick, do not overload it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each way.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, find the interjections, decide the feeling of each, read each with the right voice, and keep a steady pace.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: and, but, or, so (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

51. (2 marks)
   Answer: A capital letter begins a sentence and a full stop ends it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct use.

52. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put steps in order, begin each step with a verb, use short sentences, one action per step, add warnings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

53. (4 marks)
   Answer: I had money, so I bought bread. I wanted a toy, but it was too costly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct sentence and one for each correct comma.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each heading.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Attentive listening means choosing to give your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker so that you understand and remember what is said.
   Working / marking points: One mark for choosing to pay attention and one mark for understanding or remembering.

56. (2 marks)
   Answer: close, sit
   Working / marking points: One mark for each verb.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose a topic, a moderator and panel members, panel members give opinions in turn, the audience asks questions, the moderator summarises.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

58. (2 marks)
   Answer: on, in, under, behind, beside, between, in front of, outside (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: A dialogue is a conversation between two or more people, shown with each speaker's name and words.
   Working / marking points: One mark for conversation and one for speakers.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: Short lines, stanzas, rhyme, rhythm, images (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: It helps listeners understand and enjoy, and it helps the reader to understand the text.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each reason.
